Title: Action Research
Text / Effect: Collaborative inquiry where researchers and participants jointly investigate issues and implement change. Pros: Empowers participants; generates practical solutions; addresses real-world problems. Cons: Time-intensive; difficult to generalize; requires ongoing commitment. Use: Community development projects; institutional change initiatives.

Title: Archival Research
Text / Effect: Systematic examination of historical documents, records, and materials in archives. Pros: Access to primary sources; enables historical depth; rich contextual data. Cons: Time-consuming; documents may be incomplete or biased; limited by what was preserved. Use: Tracing institutional histories; analyzing historical discourse.

Title: Artefact Analysis
Text / Effect: Close study of material objects to understand cultural practices, values, and social relations. Pros: Reveals embodied knowledge; accesses non-textual evidence; material specificity. Cons: Requires specialist knowledge; objects may be decontextualized; preservation issues. Use: Design history; museum studies; material culture research.

Title: Autoethnography
Text / Effect: Researcher uses personal experience as primary data to analyze cultural phenomena. Pros: Insider perspective; challenges objectivity myths; accessible writing. Cons: Difficult to generalize; vulnerable self-exposure; criticized as narcissistic. Use: Identity studies; reflexive practice research; embodied experience.

Title: Biographical Method
Text / Effect: Study of individual lives through interviews, documents, and life histories to understand social and cultural contexts. Pros: Captures lived experience; reveals agency; contextualizes individual within society. Cons: Relies on memory and narration; risk of exceptionalism; time-intensive. Use: Oral history; artist biography; cultural memory studies.

Title: Case Study
Text / Effect: In-depth investigation of a single instance, event, or phenomenon within its real-world context. Pros: Rich contextual detail; good for exploratory research; captures complexity. Cons: Limited generalizability; researcher bias; labor-intensive. Use: Institutional analysis; event studies; bounded phenomena.

Title: Content Analysis
Text / Effect: Systematic coding and quantification of textual, visual, or audio material to identify patterns. Pros: Replicable; handles large datasets; reveals patterns. Cons: Decontextualizes meaning; limited depth; coding reliability issues. Use: Media representation; thematic frequency; comparative analysis.

Title: Creative Writing as Inquiry
Text / Effect: Using creative writing (fiction, poetry, hybrid forms) as a research methodology. Pros: Alternative knowledge forms; affective impact; challenges academic conventions. Cons: Evaluation criteria unclear; limited reproducibility; genre boundaries. Use: Feminist research; arts-based inquiry; representing trauma.

Title: Digital Humanities Methods
Text / Effect: Computational approaches to humanities questions (text mining, network analysis, GIS mapping). Pros: Scalable analysis; visualizes complex data; new questions. Cons: Technical barriers; loses interpretive nuance; disciplinary tensions. Use: Large-scale textual analysis; mapping spatial humanities; distant reading.

Title: Discourse Analysis
Text / Effect: Examination of language-in-use to reveal how meaning, power, and ideology are constructed. Pros: Reveals hidden power; contextual; theoretically rich. Cons: Labor-intensive; requires linguistic expertise; interpretation debates. Use: Policy analysis; media studies; critical discourse studies.

Title: Documentary Analysis
Text / Effect: Systematic examination of documents (reports, policies, media) as evidence or cultural artifacts. Pros: Non-reactive; abundant sources; historical access. Cons: Documents serve institutional agendas; authenticity issues; incomplete records. Use: Policy research; institutional critique; media archaeology.

Title: Drawing as Inquiry
Text / Effect: Using drawing practice as a mode of thinking, observing, and generating research insights. Pros: Non-verbal knowledge; observational depth; process-based thinking. Cons: Difficult to assess; subjective; requires drawing skills. Use: Design research; visual ethnography; observational studies.

Title: Embodied Mapping
Text / Effect: Creating spatial representations through bodily movement and sensory engagement with place. Pros: Captures embodied knowledge; place-specific; multi-sensory. Cons: Difficult to communicate; non-standardizable; scale limitations. Use: Urban studies; site-specific research; phenomenology of place.

Title: Ethnography
Text / Effect: Immersive fieldwork involving participant observation to understand cultural practices and meanings. Pros: Cultural depth; contextual richness; emic perspective. Cons: Time-intensive; researcher presence effects; ethical complexity. Use: Community studies; subcultural research; organizational culture.

Title: Exhibition-as-Research
Text / Effect: Using curatorial practice and exhibition-making as a mode of scholarly inquiry and argument. Pros: Public-facing research; spatial arguments; multi-modal. Cons: Resource-intensive; institutional gatekeeping; documentation challenges. Use: Curatorial research; practice-led inquiry; museum studies.

Title: Experimental Design
Text / Effect: Controlled manipulation of variables to test causal hypotheses under standardized conditions. Pros: Establishes causality; highly replicable; controls confounds. Cons: Artificial settings; ethical limits; reduces complexity. Use: Perception studies; intervention testing; controlled comparisons.

Title: Film Analysis
Text / Effect: Close reading of film texts to examine narrative, aesthetics, ideology, and cultural meaning. Pros: Multimodal richness; cultural insights; aesthetic depth. Cons: Subjective interpretation; requires film literacy; sampling issues. Use: Cinema studies; visual culture; representation analysis.

Title: Focus Groups
Text / Effect: Facilitated group discussions to explore collective meanings, attitudes, and responses. Pros: Group dynamics; generates debate; efficient data collection. Cons: Dominant voices; artificial setting; moderator effects. Use: Audience research; public engagement; exploratory studies.

Title: Grounded Theory
Text / Effect: Iterative coding of qualitative data to build theory inductively from empirical patterns. Pros: Data-driven; generates new theory; systematic process. Cons: Time-intensive; coding debates; theoretical saturation unclear. Use: Developing new concepts; understudied phenomena; process analysis.

Title: Historical Method
Text / Effect: Systematic investigation of past events through critical evaluation of primary and secondary sources. Pros: Contextualizes present; reveals change over time; critical source analysis. Cons: Source availability; historian bias; incomplete evidence. Use: Periodization; genealogies; historiography.

Title: Interview (Qualitative)
Text / Effect: Semi-structured or open-ended conversations to explore participants' experiences and perspectives. Pros: Depth and nuance; flexible; participant voice. Cons: Resource-intensive; interviewer effects; transcription labor. Use: Life histories; expert interviews; experience research.

Title: Longitudinal Study
Text / Effect: Research tracking the same subjects or phenomena over extended time periods to observe change. Pros: Captures change and development; establishes temporal patterns; controls individual variance. Cons: Attrition; resource-intensive; long timeframes. Use: Institutional evolution; cohort studies; temporal cultural change.

Title: Material Culture Analysis
Text / Effect: Interpreting the social and cultural meanings embedded in objects, design, and built environments. Pros: Accesses non-verbal culture; embodied meaning; durable evidence. Cons: Interpretive challenges; requires material knowledge; conservation access. Use: Design studies; consumption research; everyday life studies.

Title: Mixed-Methods Research
Text / Effect: Combining qualitative and quantitative approaches to leverage complementary strengths. Pros: Triangulation; comprehensive; addresses complex questions. Cons: Requires multiple skill sets; integration challenges; resource-intensive. Use: Evaluation research; complex social problems; methodological pluralism.

Title: Narrative Inquiry
Text / Effect: Analyzing stories people tell about their experiences to understand meaning-making and identity. Pros: Respects complexity; reveals subjectivity; accessible form. Cons: Constructed nature; narrative coherence bias; selection issues. Use: Life writing; illness narratives; counter-storytelling.

Title: Netnography
Text / Effect: Ethnographic study of online communities and digital cultural practices. Pros: Access to digital cultures; unobtrusive; global reach. Cons: Public/private boundaries; platform changes; disembodied interaction. Use: Online communities; digital fandom; social media culture.

Title: Oral History
Text / Effect: Recorded interviews capturing lived memories and personal testimonies of historical events. Pros: Recovers marginalized voices; experiential richness; personal testimony. Cons: Memory fallibility; subjective recall; power dynamics. Use: Community memory; counter-histories; witness testimony.

Title: Participatory Methods
Text / Effect: Research conducted collaboratively with community members as co-researchers, not subjects. Pros: Democratic; empowering; relevant to community needs. Cons: Time-intensive; power negotiations; conflicting agendas. Use: Community-based research; co-design; activist research.

Title: Performance Ethnography
Text / Effect: Embodying ethnographic insights through performance, staging research findings theatrically. Pros: Affective communication; public engagement; embodied knowledge. Cons: Representation ethics; performance skills required; documentation difficulties. Use: Applied theatre; research dissemination; activist scholarship.

Title: Phenomenology
Text / Effect: Describing lived experience as it is consciously experienced, suspending assumptions. Pros: Rich experiential detail; challenges assumptions; philosophical rigor. Cons: Difficult bracketing; relies on articulation; limited scope. Use: Embodied experience; consciousness studies; perceptual research.

Title: Practice-Based Research
Text / Effect: Creative practice itself as a mode of inquiry generating knowledge through making. Pros: Practitioner knowledge; material thinking; innovation. Cons: Evaluation challenges; documentation; articulating tacit knowledge. Use: Design research; artistic research; craft knowledge.

Title: Semiotic Analysis
Text / Effect: Reading cultural texts as systems of signs to decode underlying meanings and codes. Pros: Reveals implicit meanings; systematic; denaturalizes conventions. Cons: Requires semiotic literacy; interpretive; culturally specific. Use: Visual culture; advertising analysis; symbolic systems.

Title: Social Media Mining
Text / Effect: Harvesting and analyzing large-scale social media data for patterns and trends. Pros: Big data scale; real-time; behavioral traces. Cons: Platform bias; privacy concerns; shallow context. Use: Trend analysis; public opinion; networked communication.

Title: Soundwalk Method
Text / Effect: Attentive listening while walking through environments to understand sonic experience. Pros: Multisensory; site-specific; embodied attention. Cons: Subjective; documentation challenges; weather-dependent. Use: Sound studies; urban research; sensory ethnography.

Title: Speculative Design
Text / Effect: Creating provocative design scenarios to explore possible futures and alternative values. Pros: Opens imagination; critical reflection; engages publics. Cons: Lacks actionability; privileged speculation; evaluation unclear. Use: Design futures; critical design; ethical speculation.

Title: Statistical Analysis
Text / Effect: Mathematical analysis of numerical data to test hypotheses and identify significant patterns. Pros: Rigor; falsifiable; comparative. Cons: Reduces complexity; requires large samples; statistical literacy. Use: Survey analysis; comparative studies; hypothesis testing.

Title: Survey (Quantitative)
Text / Effect: Standardized questionnaires distributed to large samples to measure variables systematically. Pros: Generalizable; efficient; quantifiable. Cons: Shallow data; response bias; assumes shared meanings. Use: Population attitudes; demographic patterns; large-scale comparison.

Title: Textual Analysis
Text / Effect: Close interpretive reading of written texts to analyze meaning, rhetoric, and ideology. Pros: Depth of interpretation; textual nuance; critical reading. Cons: Subjective; labor-intensive; sampling limitations. Use: Literary criticism; rhetorical analysis; ideological critique.

Title: Thematic Analysis
Text / Effect: Identifying and analyzing recurring themes and patterns across qualitative data. Pros: Flexible; accessible; systematic organization. Cons: Atheoretical; risks decontextualization; researcher interpretation. Use: Interview analysis; qualitative coding; pattern identification.

Title: VR Ethnography
Text / Effect: Using virtual reality environments for ethnographic research or immersive data representation. Pros: Novel environments; immersive; spatial data. Cons: Technology barriers; embodiment questions; expensive. Use: Virtual worlds; immersive journalism; spatial storytelling.

Title: Visual Analysis
Text / Effect: Systematic interpretation of images, photographs, art, or visual media. Pros: Accesses visual culture; revealing; material specificity. Cons: Subjective interpretation; requires visual literacy; cultural context. Use: Art history; visual culture; photographic archives.

Title: Walking Interview
Text / Effect: Conducting interviews while walking with participants through meaningful places. Pros: Place-based insights; embodied memory; dynamic. Cons: Recording difficulties; physical access; weather-dependent. Use: Place attachment; memory studies; urban research.

Title: Experiments
Text / Effect: Controlled studies testing causal relationships by manipulating independent variables. Pros: Establishes causation; controlled; replicable. Cons: Artificial; limited ecological validity; reductionist. Use: Perceptual psychology; A/B testing; intervention effects.

Title: Forensic Aesthetics
Text / Effect: Critical investigation using aesthetic analysis of material evidence to challenge official narratives. Pros: Visual evidence; counter-narratives; spatial reconstruction. Cons: Requires technical expertise; contested authority; resource-intensive. Use: Human rights investigation; spatial analysis; architectural evidence.

Title: Statistical Modelling
Text / Effect: Building mathematical models to represent relationships between variables and predict outcomes. Pros: Predictive power; handles complexity; testable. Cons: Model assumptions; interpretability; data requirements. Use: Predictive analysis; pattern modeling; computational humanities.
